summary: V.S. Industry Berhad, an investment holding company, engages in the manufacturing, assembling and selling electronic and electrical products, and plastic molded components and parts. It offers electronics manufacturing services for office and household electrical and electronic products. Its manufacturing solutions include product design services; mold design and fabrication services; PCBA, electronics, and mechanics manufacturing services; plastic injection/finishing processing services; final assembly, box built, and testing services; and supply chain management services. It also provides OEM/ODM services covering the project life cycle in various sectors of industries, such as audio, computers, telecommunications, automobile, and other industries. In addition, the company involved in the design and fabrication of driver safety products, screen fabric printing, filter components, and other related products; design and sell healthcare products; trading of electronic products, screen printing equipment, materials, kits, and driver safety products; and provision of hostel management services, as well as offers treasury and financing services. It operates in Malaysia, the United States, Indonesia, Philippines, Europe, the People's Republic of China, Singapore, and internationally. V.S. Industry Berhad was founded in 1979 and is headquartered in Senai, Malaysia.

report.summary: V.S. Industry Berhad (VS) is Malaysia's largest electronic manufacturing services (EMS) provider, assembling consumer electronics, household appliances, and industrial components. The group recently recorded its first full-year net loss since listing in 1998 amid an inventory correction and weak end-consumer spending, which compressed margins into negative territory (-1.47%). However, the balance sheet remains sound with RM663.1 million in cash offsetting RM664.0 million in total debt, and the stock trades at an attractive 0.62x price-to-book value (RM0.535 book value per share). Following a sharp 73.7% rebound over the past six months from its 52-week low of RM0.170 to RM0.330, near-term upside appears capped by key resistance at RM0.365 until tangible order recoveries emerge. We rate VS a Hold with an accumulation bias on pullbacks toward RM0.260-RM0.275.

business.what_they_do: V.S. Industry is a full-fledged turnkey Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) provider. The company provides end-to-end manufacturing solutions including mold design, plastic injection molding, printed circuit board assembly (PCBA), and full box-build assembly for global electronic brands.
segments: Malaysia operations (core contributor, historically generating >70% of revenue across electronics, electrical, and plastic components)
China operations (printed circuit boards and plastic molding, historically scaled down)
Philippines and International operations (emerging manufacturing footprints and trading)
business.customers_and_markets: VS serves international brand owners across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. Key end-markets include floor care appliances, smart home products, pool cleaning robotics, and consumer audio/beverage systems.
business.competitive_position: VS is the largest listed EMS player on Bursa Malaysia by revenue and capacity, competing primarily with domestic peers such as SKP Resources, ATA IMS, and Aurelius Technologies, as well as regional EMS giants in Vietnam and China. Its scale and vertically integrated capabilities allow it to handle complex high-volume turnkey assembly.
business.moat: Narrow moat derived from high customer switching costs and high capital expenditure barriers in vertical integration (tooling, injection molding, cleanrooms, and testing certifications). However, contract pricing power is constrained by major brand owners who frequently negotiate cost-downs.

report.management_and_ownership: The company was founded in 1979 and is led by Executive Chairman Mr. Kim Ling Beh and Managing Director Mr. Sem Yam Gan. Insiders hold a significant 23.75% equity stake, aligning leadership with shareholders, while institutional investors hold 26.81%, reflecting strong domestic institutional coverage.

financial_health.growth: Revenue contracted from RM4.56 billion in FY23 to RM4.25 billion in FY24 and RM3.79 billion in FY25, while net profit fell from RM246.0 million in FY24 to RM36.7 million in FY25 before sliding into quarterly losses in early FY26.
financial_health.profitability: Margins have deteriorated severely with gross margin at 3.17%, operating margin at -1.30%, and net profit margin at -1.47%, pulling return on equity (ROE) down to -2.62%.
financial_health.balance_sheet: The balance sheet remains resilient with total cash of RM663.1 million against total debt of RM664.0 million (nearly neutral net debt position) and a healthy current ratio of 1.98x alongside debt-to-equity of 32.22%.
financial_health.cash_flow: Operating cash flow remains positive at RM211.5 million over the trailing period (RM616.1 million in FY25), though free cash flow was slightly negative at -RM14.8 million after capital expenditures.
financial_health.dividends: Dividends per share have stepped down alongside earnings from RM0.025 in 2024 to RM0.010 in 2025 and RM0.004 in 2026, offering a modest trailing dividend yield of 1.21%.

recent_developments: 2026-10-01: The Star reported that VS Industry is poised for an earnings recovery in FY27 as order flows stabilize across core customer product lines.
2026-09-30: The Edge Malaysia and Traders Union reported that VS surged to a six-month high after 4Q and full-year losses came in smaller than market consensus had feared.
2026-09-30: HLIB research raised its outlook on VS Industry despite the FY26 net loss, citing inventory normalization at key customers.
2026-09-30: Maybank Research upgraded VS Industry from Sell to Hold with an updated target price of RM0.250 (reported via Moomoo).

2026-09-29: The Malaysian Reserve and The Edge Malaysia reported that VS Industry posted its first full-year net loss since its 1998 Bursa listing due to customer inventory de-stocking and suppressed demand.

valuation.current: VS trades at RM0.330, lacking a trailing P/E ratio due to recent quarterly losses (TTM EPS -RM0.01), but sits at a forward P/E of 12.76x based on FY27 turnaround estimates. It trades at a substantial 38% discount to book value (P/B 0.62x vs BVPS of RM0.535), reflecting deep cyclical pessimism.

scenarios.assumptions: Protracted consumer demand slump leaves FY27 recovery sluggish with normalized EPS of RM0.018 valued at 12.0x forward P/E, or approximately 0.40x-0.45x book value (RM0.535 BVPS), re-testing support at RM0.210.

Customer order restocking drives modest recovery to EPS of RM0.026 (matching the implied forward P/E of 12.8x at current price) valued at 13.0x forward P/E = RM0.338, or 0.65x book value, near resistance of RM0.365.
Robust restocking cycle and onboarding of new customers ramp EPS back toward RM0.035, valued at 13.5x forward P/E = RM0.473, approaching 0.90x book value and closer to the 52-week high of RM0.545.

bull_case: Cyclical recovery: As global customer inventories normalize, order volumes from major brand partners are positioned to rebound into FY27.
Asset protection: Trading at 0.62x P/B with RM0.535 book value per share and nearly zero net debt provides a substantial valuation floor.
Operating leverage: Turnkey EMS facilities have high fixed overheads; any volume ramp-up will drive rapid gross margin expansion from the current depressed 3.17%.
bear_case: Prolonged consumer discretionary weakness: S&P 500 and western consumer spending trends remain subdued, delaying major product line replenishment.
Margin squeeze: Sub-optimal plant utilization and labor costs may continue to generate operating losses if quarterly revenues remain stuck near RM770-800 million.
Customer concentration risk: High dependence on a few anchor customers leaves earnings vulnerable to unilateral design phase-outs or contract reallocations.
catalysts: Upcoming quarterly earnings releases confirming sequential gross margin expansion and a return to net profitability.
Announcement of major contract wins or new product model assembly allocations in Senai or regional facilities.
Strengthening US consumer spending data or a rebound in USD/MYR improving export realization.
risks: Risk of extended operational losses if end-customer sales continue to miss forecasts.
Currency volatility, as export revenues are USD-denominated while manufacturing costs are primarily in Ringgit.
Supply chain delays or raw material price inflation eroding paper-thin contract margins.

verdict.summary: VS is an established cyclical EMS leader emerging from its worst trough since 1998, well-backed by a clean balance sheet and a deep 0.62x P/B discount. However, after rallying 73.7% in six months to RM0.330, the shares are approaching stiff technical resistance at RM0.365 while earnings remain in the red. Investors with a 6-24 month view should wait for pullbacks toward moving average support before initiating new positions.
verdict.entry_plan: Accumulate on retracements toward RM0.265-RM0.276 (confluence of SMA50 at RM0.265 and SMA200 at RM0.276). Strong secondary accumulation zone lies near the 3-month support of RM0.210.
verdict.invalidation: Thesis breaks if quarterly operating cash flows turn decisively negative or if the stock breaks decisively below its 52-week low of RM0.170, signaling structural customer loss.

verify_yourself: Examine the latest quarterly notes (Notes to Interim Financial Report) to verify whether gross profit margins have turned positive from the -RM8.6 million recorded in 3Q.
Check customer concentration metrics in Note 33/Segment Information of the latest Annual Report to gauge exposure to top two clients.
Track cash and borrowing balances in subsequent Bursa quarterlies to ensure the near-neutral net debt position (RM663m cash vs RM664m debt) is maintained.
Review Bursa announcements for any insider acquisitions or disposals by executive directors Beh Kim Ling and Gan Sem Yam.
